messages:
tara: PSA I opened a docs PR to refresh the model card for zephyr-7b-q4 — clarifies supported builds, effective context limits for quantized variants, new bench table, and a short SDK migration section. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4920

james: thanks. can we make the SDK streaming example show the new iterator pattern for both py/js? people keep using old .stream arg.

leila: noted. also found the current card lists 32k context for all builds — for q4 we should say "~28k effective (depends on quantization and kv-cache)". will add a short note under "limits".

ryan: can you add a hardware column to the bench? include A100-80GB, A10G, and a CPU-quant run (int8). otherwise numbers are misleading.

tara: current bench snippet in the PR (placeholder):```bash
# bench (local) commit: a1b2c3d
# A100-80GB, batch=1, seq=2048
./bench --model zephyr-7b-q4 --seq 2048 --hw a100
# out: 9.8 tok/s, p50 22ms, p95 70ms
```

james: can we convert that to a compact table in the card and include exact bench command + commit sha? docs readers copy those commands directly.

leila: drafting the SDK migration bullets. proposal: "SDK migration (quick)": - Python: client.generate(..., response_mode='stream') and iterate: async for chunk in resp: print(chunk.text) - JS: replace stream: true with response_mode: 'stream' and for-await-of on the response - CLI: `redwood infer --stream -> --response-mode stream` Keep each bullet 1 line.

ryan: small nit: call it `effective context` phrase and link to a short explainer about kv-cache/quantization tradeoffs.

docs-bot: build/docs: #4920 — linkcheck failed on /model-catalog/zephyr-7b-q4.html#limits (404)

tara: I pushed a tiny anchor rename fix and added the commit sha for the bench. Please re-run linkcheck.

docs-bot: build/docs: #4920 — linkcheck passed

james: review incoming. I'll tidy the JS snippet to match the SDK samples page and add the small diff.

leila: added the effective-context wording + one-sentence explainer about why quantized builds lose a few thousand tokens. Also added the CPU run numbers (approx).

ryan: LGTM on benches and notes. small suggestion: add a one-line "compatibility" row: supported runtimes (onnx, triton, cuda) and known caveats.

tara: updated compatibility row and added a 3-bullet migration guide at the bottom (breaking changes, sdk snippet migration, effective limits). Keeping it short so other model-card PRs can copy it.

docs-bot: build/docs: #4920 — merged by tara (after approvals).
